title: Multiplexed streaming load driver for realistic SSE/WebSocket chat scenarios
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a production-grade load testing harness that emulates realistic streaming chat/completion traffic over both Server-Sent Events (SSE) and WebSocket transports. The driver will focus on precise token/sec measurement, p95/p99 latency tracking at token and message boundaries, and statistical regression detection for tail latency and throughput. This harness must support: multiplexing multiple chat sessions per connection, configurable think-time distributions, controllable network jitter and packet loss, KV-cache warmup scenarios, and backpressure simulation. Outputs should be Prometheus-compatible metrics and annotated traces for linking to existing console dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: Driver can simultaneously maintain 10k active connections (SSE) with 50k concurrent chat sessions multiplexed and report tokens/sec with <2% measurement error
p95 and p99 token-latencies are computed and emitted per-model and per-connection-tag to Prometheus every 10s

Regression detection engine flags anomalies using both delta-thresholds and an adaptive statistical test (e.g., bootstrap / Mann-Whitney) and can post alerts to #perf-alerts Slack and create a linked incident in PagerDuty
Support end-to-end metrics: first-byte latency, per-token inter-arrival distribution, stream-end latency, and incremental cost estimate (tokens * model-rate) for each run
Reference workload suite (20 synthetic user scenarios) checked in and runnable via ./bin/loaddriver --scenario <name>
Integration with runtime tracing: each synthetic session attaches trace context so e2e traces appear in console and link to Prometheus metrics
tasks: Design multiplexing protocol for SSE (comment tags) and WebSocket (subprotocol or JSON envelope) — include reconnect semantics
Implement client emulator in Rust with Tokio for high concurrency, token-level timers, and pluggable network impairments
Add measurement library that records token emission times, chunk sizes, and partial message receipts to compute token/sec and p95 token latency
Expose metrics via Prometheus endpoint and push summaries to existing perf dashboard (grafana.redwood.internal/perf-load)
Implement regression detector service that ingests run summaries and historical baselines and emits alerts
Create 20 scenario specifications (mix of short bursts, long-running multi-turn, KV-cache-warmup, and fanout-to-multiple-models)
Write CI job that runs a representative medium load (smoke) on every runtime change and fails on regressions above configured thresholds
Document runbook and example analysis notebook for troubleshooting spikes and false positives
